cases.title: Compaction silently drops an early tool contract

versions.change: Baseline agent with full-history prompting.
Add line-range file viewing to reduce irrelevant tool output.
Compact history after 80k tokens by summarizing only user and assistant messages.
versions.patch:
+ kept = [m for m in history if m.role in ('user', 'assistant')]
+ summary = summarize(kept)
+ history = [summary]

versions.change: Add targeted retry prompts after a failed test command.
Add a faster repository index used only for file discovery.

failure.error: The agent edits generated files despite an earlier tool result marking them read-only, then fails the final repository integrity check.
observations: The failure appears only after the conversation crosses the compaction threshold.
Short runs on the same task family still pass.
The v3 retry logic repeats the forbidden edit instead of recovering.
debug: Before compaction, message 41 is a tool result: READ_ONLY_PATHS=['src/generated/**'].
The compacted history contains no tool-result messages and no READ_ONLY_PATHS marker.
The first forbidden edit occurs immediately after compaction; the repository index resolves the path correctly.

oracle.explanation: v2 removes tool-result contracts during compaction; later changes only expose or repeat the latent defect.

cases.title: A cache key omits repository identity

versions.change: Baseline agent without tool-result caching.
Normalize tool arguments before logging for stable traces.
Add explicit repository IDs to session metadata.
Cache read-only tool results by tool name and canonical arguments.
Run two independent task sessions concurrently.
Add progress events around concurrent task execution.

failure.error: A Django task receives the contents of requests/sessions.py from a different repository and patches a nonexistent symbol.
observations: The error requires two repositories with the same relative file path to run concurrently.
Sequential single-repository evaluations pass.
The wrong content is returned by the read_file tool before any model reasoning error.
debug: Both reads use key read_file:{"path":"src/sessions.py"}.
Session repo IDs differ, but repo_id is absent from the cache key.
The second read is logged cache_hit=true and its result hash equals the first repository's file.

oracle.explanation: v3 introduces a cross-repository cache collision; concurrency in v4 makes it observable.

cases.title: A retry loop resets useful partial progress

versions.change: Baseline single-attempt coding agent.
Validate that generated patches touch a non-test source file.
versions.patch: + valid = any(not is_test(path) for path in changed_files)

versions.change: Retry invalid patches up to three times, resetting the repository before each retry.
versions.patch:
+ for attempt in range(3):
+     git_reset_hard(base_commit)
+     patch = run_agent(problem)

versions.change: Feed the previous test failure into the next retry prompt.
Add a final syntax check before returning the selected patch.

failure.error: The final patch fixes the caller but omits the helper function created during the first attempt, causing NameError: normalize_field is not defined.
observations: Attempt 1 creates normalize_field but fails a caller-side assertion.
Attempt 2 fixes the caller and passes the local syntax check.
The final diff contains only the attempt-2 edit.
debug: git diff before retry 2 contains utils.py:+def normalize_field(...).
git reset --hard runs before retry 2 and removes that diff.
The retry prompt includes the assertion text but not the discarded patch or helper definition.

oracle.explanation: v2 makes retries destructive; v3 adds feedback but does not preserve prior useful edits.

cases.title: A framework-specific validator is inserted into the global loop

versions.change: Baseline coding agent.
Add structured diff parsing for modified files.
Add a generic post-patch review hook, disabled by default.
Register Django migration regex checks globally and force a revision on any match.
Improve revision prompts with line-numbered diff context.

failure.error: A correct patch in a non-Django ORM project is replaced by a revision that removes a required field option.
observations: The first generated patch passes all project tests.
The forced revision is the only patch returned to evaluation.
Disabling review hooks makes the same model output pass.
debug: DjangoPatternChecker matches the string 'models.CharField' in a compatibility fixture.
Repository inspection finds no manage.py, django dependency, or migrations package.
Revision trace says 'remove unsupported null=True'; the target ORM requires null=True.

oracle.explanation: v3 activates a domain-specific checker globally; v4 only makes its incorrect revision more targeted.

cases.title: Parallel tool execution violates a write-then-read dependency

versions.change: Baseline serial tool dispatcher.
Classify tools as read-only or mutating.
versions.patch: + tool.effect = READ_ONLY if name in READ_TOOLS else MUTATING

versions.change: Execute all tool calls in one assistant message concurrently.
versions.patch: + results = await gather(*(call(tool) for tool in tool_calls))

versions.change: Add a test-result parser for faster failure summaries.
Stream tool completion events to the transcript.

failure.error: The agent reports tests passing for the pre-edit code, but the submitted patch fails those same tests.
observations: The assistant emits write_file followed by run_tests in one message.
The failure is intermittent and more common on a cold filesystem.
Serial execution removes the mismatch.
debug: run_tests starts at 10:03:11.204; write_file finishes at 10:03:11.287.
Test trace reads file hash 9ab1; submitted workspace after tools has hash f042.
Both calls are scheduled by the same gather() despite one being mutating.

oracle.explanation: v2 ignores tool dependencies and introduces the race; later observability changes do not cause it.

cases.title: Session summaries omit tool error state

versions.change: Baseline agent with raw transcript replay.
Store tool names and text output in a compact event schema.
Add branch summaries generated from compact events.
Use branch summaries when resuming after context compaction.
Include modified file names in each compact tool event.
Add a concise final-answer template.
versions.patch: + final_prompt = 'Report tests and changed files concisely.'

failure.error: After compaction, the agent states that the integration test passed even though the test command exited 1.
observations: The raw pre-compaction transcript contains the correct nonzero exit status.
The resumed branch summary quotes stdout but labels it as a normal tool observation.
The final-answer template trusts the resumed summary.
debug: Raw event has is_error=true and exit_code=1.
The compact event schema contains only tool, text, and paths; neither is_error nor exit_code is serialized.
The first version introducing compact events is v1; later summary/resume steps propagate the lost state.

oracle.explanation: v1 irreversibly drops error metadata before summarization; v2/v3 expose the latent loss.

cases.title: Resolved paths are cached without the working directory

versions.change: Baseline path resolution per tool call.
Normalize relative paths before filesystem access.
Fork a fresh workspace for each benchmark task.
Memoize normalized relative paths by their input string.
Reuse one worker process across several isolated task sessions.

failure.error: An edit intended for task B is applied to task A's temporary checkout.
observations: Both tasks request the relative path src/config.py.
Each task has a distinct isolated cwd.
The failure requires worker reuse; a fresh process per task passes.
debug: Task A caches src/config.py -> /tmp/task-a/src/config.py.
Task B cache lookup uses only 'src/config.py' and returns the task-A absolute path.
The workspace guard runs before cache lookup, not after the cached path is returned.

oracle.explanation: v3 omits cwd/session identity from the cache key; v4 worker reuse reveals the collision.

cases.title: A static allowlist hides dynamically loaded tools

versions.change: Baseline tool registry exposes all loaded tools.
Add extension reload without restarting the session.
Record each tool's source extension for audit logs.
Add a static startup allowlist to reduce tool-selection tokens.
versions.patch: + visible_tools = [t for t in registry if t.name in startup_allowlist]

versions.change: Load a repository-specific symbol-search extension after startup.

failure.error: The model cannot call symbol_search and repeatedly scans files manually until it exhausts the turn budget.
observations: The extension loader reports symbol-search loaded successfully.
The tool is present in the runtime registry.
The model's advertised tool schema does not include symbol_search.
debug: startup_allowlist is captured before the extension reload.
visible_tools is not recomputed after registry change events.
Removing the startup allowlist exposes symbol_search immediately.

oracle.explanation: v3 freezes tool visibility at startup; v4 is a valid extension whose tool is shadowed.

cases.title: The context budget ignores cache-read tokens

versions.change: Baseline context budgeting from total provider usage.
Split usage reporting into input, output, cache-read, and cache-write fields.
Trigger compaction using input plus output tokens only.
versions.patch:
+ consumed = usage.input + usage.output
+ if consumed > limit: compact()

versions.change: Enable provider prefix caching for repository context.
Attach more repository documentation to the cached prefix.

failure.error: Provider rejects the final request with context_length_exceeded although the harness reports 124k/180k tokens used.
observations: The failure begins after prefix caching is enabled and repository docs grow.
Turning off caching makes the harness compact earlier and the request succeeds.
No individual new message is unusually large.
debug: Usage at failure: input=118k, output=6k, cache_read=71k, cache_write=0.
Harness consumed calculation is 118k+6k=124k; provider context occupancy is about 195k.
The consumed formula was introduced before prefix caching and omits cache_read.

oracle.explanation: v2 undercounts context occupancy; v3/v4 increase the omitted cache-read component.

cases.title: Patch validation rejects a valid deletion-only fix

versions.change: Baseline agent returns its first patch.
Parse changed paths from unified diff headers.
Reject patches unless the parsed paths include a non-test source file.
versions.patch: + if not any(is_source(p) for p in paths): retry()

versions.change: Add a clearer retry message explaining that source code must change.
versions.patch: + retry_reason = 'Modify at least one non-test source file.'

versions.change: Select the last retry that passes syntax validation.

failure.error: The correct deletion of obsolete.py is discarded; a later retry edits an unrelated caller and fails regression tests.
observations: The task is solved by deleting a deprecated module that is auto-discovered at runtime.
Attempt 1 exactly matches the reference deletion.
Attempts 2 and 3 are generated only because attempt 1 is labeled invalid.
debug: A deleted file's unified diff header is '+++ /dev/null', so the v1 parser returns no b/... path.
The v2 validator sees paths=[] and rejects the patch.
The syntax validator in v4 cannot evaluate a deleted file and therefore selects the unrelated retry.

oracle.explanation: v1 first introduces the latent inability to represent deletion paths; v2 later turns that pre-existing defect into a blocking gate.

cases.title: The latest reload change advertises a stale tool schema

versions.change: Baseline extension loader with session restart.
Add stable extension IDs to resource metadata.
Support extension reload inside an existing session.
Invalidate the visible tool list after every successful reload.
Reuse the pre-reload JSON schema object when a tool name is unchanged.

failure.error: After reload, the model calls symbol_search with the old 'query' argument, but the updated extension requires 'pattern'.
observations: The tool implementation and runtime registry both use the new pattern argument.
Starting a fresh session advertises the correct schema.
Only same-session reloads after v4 fail.
debug: Reload log: tool name unchanged, old schema object reused.
Advertised schema contains required=['query']; runtime validator contains required=['pattern'].
v3 clears the tool-list cache correctly; v4 repopulates it with the stale object.

oracle.explanation: The most recent v4 optimization directly introduces the stale-schema mismatch.

cases.title: The latest timeout refactor mixes seconds and milliseconds

versions.change: Baseline shell tool with a fixed timeout.
Expose per-command timeout in tool arguments.
Add progress heartbeats while shell commands run.
Allow test commands to request up to ten minutes.
Record timeout values in run telemetry.
Pass the timeout to a new subprocess helper that expects milliseconds.

failure.error: A test command requesting 300 seconds is killed after about 300 milliseconds.
observations: The command consistently terminates before its first one-second heartbeat.
v4 runs the same command for the requested five minutes.
The failure affects every command with an explicit timeout.
debug: Telemetry records timeout_seconds=300.
New helper trace records timeout_ms=300 and sends SIGTERM at 0.301 seconds.
No earlier version calls the millisecond-based helper.

oracle.explanation: The latest edge passes seconds directly to a millisecond API.
